# backend

<!-- layer1:start · generated by the harness · do not edit by hand -->

## Verification

1. **Verify before asserting, and with whatever consumes it.** Never take a
   file's word about the environment: **run the tool that reads it and trigger
   what it controls.** What cannot be checked stays `❓ pending`, said out loud.

   _Asking is not enough: `pnpm config get` answered `42` for a key that does
   not exist, and `true` for one that changed nothing._

2. **"Done" means verified by CI, not asserted.** What has not passed the gate
   stays pending, and that is said.

   _A green on your machine only proves your machine._

## What the AI does not decide

3. **`.env`, credentials and real data dumps: neither read without explicit
   permission, nor committed.** What the agent reads **enters the
   conversation**, and from there it does not come back. `.env.example` is what
   travels.

4. **The AI installs and configures nothing on its own**: it proposes, the owner
   decides.

   _An install or a config change lands in everyone's lockfile and CI, and
   neither shows in the diff the agent presents._

5. **Nothing destructive without a `--dry-run` first**, showing what would be
   deleted.

   _A `git clean -fd` took three unrecoverable directories._

6. **The AI commits; the person decides the push.** Local commits pile up until
   the go-ahead, **and one go-ahead covers one push**, not the next ones.

7. **No AI trace in commits or output**: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated
   with…".

   _Tools add it by default. History says what changed and why, not with which
   tool._

8. **Conventional Commits, in English**: `type(scope): summary`, with `!` for a
   breaking change. The types: `feat` · `fix` · `docs` · `style` · `refactor` ·
   `perf` · `test` · `build` · `ci` · `chore` · `revert`. The body carries
   **only** the list of changes and the reason for each — the how is already in
   the diff.

## The environment

9. **An agent session has no Node auto-switch.** The hook lives in the shell
   profile and a non-interactive session never loads it: the session runs on
   whatever Node it **inherited when it was launched**, and `cd` into another
   project does not change it.

   **Start the session from a terminal already on the repo's version** — enter
   the directory, let fnm/nvm switch, then launch the agent. **One session per
   project.**

   _If that was not done, activate it on every invocation: `fnm use <major>`
   then the command. `fnm exec --using=N pnpm` does not work on Windows — `pnpm`
   is a `.cmd` and `fnm exec` only launches real executables._

10. **pnpm, never npm.**

_`npm install` leaves a `package-lock.json` next to `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and two
installers disagree in silence._

11. **pnpm settings live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`**; `.npmrc` carries registry
    and authentication only — from pnpm 11 anything else there is ignored, and
    pnpm 10 still reads it, so it works today and stops on upgrade. Every repo
    with dependencies sets `minimumReleaseAge` there.

## Continuity

12. **State lives in `docs/SESSION.md`**, written **when a task closes** — at
    session close there is no context left — and **overwritten**: git keeps the
    history. Nothing the code or `git log` already tells goes in.

13. **The reasoning lives in `docs/DECISIONS.md`**, append-only. A decision that
    changes **is not edited**: another is appended revising it, and the old one
    is **marked, never deleted**. Knowing what was believed is part of the
    record.

14. **An exception is declared** in the project's `AGENTS.md`, with its reason
    and its scope; failing silently is not an option. Does not apply to
    security, AI traces or pushing.

## Naming

15. **File names, configuration keys and identifiers in English.**

## Knowledge that is not in this file

16. **Skills are per project.** `npx autoskills` installs them into
    `<repo>/.claude/skills/`, which is **git-ignored and rebuilt** like
    `node_modules`; **`skills-lock.json` is committed** — it carries each
    skill's source and hash, and it is what makes three machines rebuild the
    same set. **The developer runs `autoskills`, not the agent** — `npx`
    downloads a package, and installing is not the agent's call.

_Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` are the machine's, not the project's._

17. **Official docs and MCPs are consulted and never silenced**, at the
    **installed** version — from the lockfile, not the `^` range. **Context7 is
    the one every project uses**: `resolve-library-id`, then `query-docs` at
    that version. If the MCP does not answer, say so instead of pretending it
    was consulted.

## Review

18. **When work is reviewed, this is the shape.** `architect` before building;
    `reviewer` and `security` over what was built, **read-only**; `tester` to
    verify. Run them whenever you want, together or on their own.

`backend/` is one of two independent pnpm projects inside the `Four-Points` repo
(the other is `frontend/`). The root [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) holds what both
share — Context7 policy, Markdown formatting, commits and hooks, the security
level, the frontend ↔ backend contract and the module map — and is loaded
through the root `CLAUDE.md`. OpenCode started inside `backend/` loads only this
file: read the root one too.

This file also covers the stack, commands, architecture and module docs of
`backend/`. Paths are relative to `backend/` unless they start with `frontend/`.

## Exceptions

- **Rules 12 and 13 — state and decisions live at the repo root.** They are
  `docs/SESSION.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` in the root, shared with
  `frontend/`. `backend/docs/` is git-ignored (`backend/.gitignore:127`) and is
  not used for them.

## Security

**L3** — estimated on 2026-09-28: there is login and user accounts, personal
data (users, guest blacklist with photos, cashier) and own backend; the L3 level
is declared by the owner as the target (`docs/DECISIONS.md` ADR-017), not the
current state. **Re-estimate when:** Aiven starts storing real guest or staff
data.

The level line is the same in the root `AGENTS.md`; a re-estimate changes both.
Paths below are relative to `backend/`.

**Areas:**

- Authentication, Session, JWT tokens → `controllers/auth/`, `services/auth/`,
  `middlewares/authenticateToken.ts`
- Authorization → `middlewares/roleCheck.ts`, `middlewares/demoRestriction.ts`;
  object-level authorization lives in controllers (e.g. `controllers/messages/`)
  and in `WHERE` clauses of `repositories/`
- API, Validation / errors → `routes/`, `controllers/`, `validations/`,
  `index.ts`
- File upload → `middlewares/imageUpload.ts` and
  `middlewares/backofficeUpload.ts` (routes `auth`, `backoffice`, `checklist`,
  `maintenance`); multer directly in `routes/blacklist/` and `routes/fnb/`
- Data protection / privacy → `blacklist`, `cashier`, users
  (`repositories/auth/`), parking vehicles (`parking_vehicles`) and messaging
  (`repositories/messages/`)
- Configuration / DevOps → `config/`, `.env*`
- Logging / monitoring → `config/logger.ts`; business audit trail in
  `services/logbook/` and `repositories/logbook/logbookHistory-repository.ts`
- Validation / errors (data access) → `repositories/` and the triggers and
  procedures in `db-mysql/` (parking availability, booking code)

## Where the model goes wrong

- **A prompt that asks for several tasks at once** → work them **one at a
  time**, each with the context specific to it, when the work touches code.

## Stack

- **Express 5.1.0** on Node 22 (`.nvmrc`, `engines: 22.x`), pnpm 10.28.0.
- **TypeScript 5.9.3**, ES modules (`"type": "module"`), run directly by **tsx**
  — no compile step. `pnpm build` only creates the Python venv for the
  scheduling solver; it is Render's build command.
- **MySQL** through `mysql2`, against a local DB or Aiven (cloud).
- **Zod 4** for validation, **Vitest** for tests, **pino** for logs.
- **Cloudinary** for images and PDFs. No email sending: `email-service.ts` and
  `nodemailer` were removed on 2026-10-02.

Lower risk, but verify when touched: `node-cron` 4.2.1, `express-rate-limit`
8.2.1, `helmet` 8.1.0, `pino` 10.3.1, `archiver` 7.0.1, `mysql2` 3.14.2,
`jsonwebtoken` 9.0.2.

## Commands

```bash
pnpm dev              # tsx watch; DB from DB_ENVIRONMENT (default local)
pnpm dev:local        # local MySQL
pnpm dev:aiven        # Aiven cloud DB
pnpm start            # without watch
pnpm setup:local      # fresh local install: tables, first admin, departments, mock data
pnpm typecheck        # tsc --noEmit
pnpm lint             # ESLint
pnpm format           # Prettier (format:check to only check)
pnpm test             # all tests with Vitest (test:watch, test:coverage)
pnpm test:corpus      # scheduling corpus only
pnpm verify           # lint + format:check + typecheck + test — what CI runs
```

The port comes from `PORT` (4000 in `.env.example`; the code falls back to
3000). `demo:user`, `demo:user:aiven` and `seed:scheduling:export` are one-off
scripts in `scripts/`.

## Architecture

```
index.ts → routes → controllers → services → repositories → models
                         ↓
                    validations (Zod)
```

- **Imports use the `.js` extension** even for `.ts` files:
  `import { x } from './file.js'`, never `'./file'`.
- **One folder per domain in each layer**: `routes/<domain>/`,
  `controllers/<domain>/`, `services/<domain>/`, `repositories/<domain>/`,
  `validations/`, `models/<domain>/`.
- **Database**: the pool is in `config/db.ts`; `config/db-config.ts` picks the
  connection by `DB_ENVIRONMENT` (`local` by default, or `aiven`). Transactions
  through `config/transaction.ts`.
- **Errors**: Express 5 forwards async errors to the global handler in
  `index.ts`; module-specific codes in `config/error-codes.ts`.
- **CORS** (`config/cors.ts`): a fixed list of origins — `localhost:3000`
  outside production, the production and Vercel domains — plus `FRONTEND_URL`.
  Credentials enabled. It is also the CSRF defence: any other origin gets a 403
  before reaching a route.
- **Cron jobs**: `services/cron/cron-service.ts`, started from `index.ts`.
- **Tests**: Vitest, in `tests/`, one folder per domain.

## Authentication

The contract with the frontend is in the root `AGENTS.md`; here, where it lives.

- **JWT** (`jsonwebtoken`), signed with `SECRET_JWT_KEY`, stateless — no DB
  lookup per request. The cookies are set in
  `controllers/auth/auth-controllers.ts`; `COOKIE_DOMAIN` applies only in
  production.
- **`middlewares/authenticateToken.ts`** reads the `access_token` cookie
  (`Authorization: Bearer` as fallback), verifies it and then runs
  `demoRestriction`.
- **Roles** are enforced in `middlewares/roleCheck.ts` (`canManageGroups`,
  `canAccessFnb`…). Object-level checks live in controllers and in the `WHERE`
  clauses of `repositories/`.
- **Demo** (ADR-038): only with `DEMO_MODE=true`. The account is an admin with
  `users.is_demo = 1`, carried in the token; `middlewares/demoRestriction.ts`
  blocks what the demo must not touch, and a route that writes outside what the
  daily reset restores needs its own `denyDemo` / `denyDemoWrites` guard. There
  is no `demo-admin` role any more.
- **Never reintroduce** `express-session`, `req.session` or a `sessions` table:
  they were planned once and dropped.

## Database

- Database `hotel_db`, local and on Aiven — **both have data**.
- ⚠️ **Never** run `MASTER_INSTALL*.sql` or `db-mysql/aiven/NN_*.sql` against
  them: first-install scripts only. A fresh install is `pnpm setup:local`.
- Any schema change goes in a new idempotent `db-mysql/scripts/YYYYMMDD_*.sql`,
  applied to local and Aiven, plus a row in the "Migraciones incrementales"
  table of `db-mysql/INDEX.md`.
- Policy, schema overview, roles and backups:
  [`db-mysql/AGENTS.md`](db-mysql/AGENTS.md). Read it before touching any table.

## Messaging

No module doc yet. Internal messages between staff: `controllers/messages/`,
`repositories/messages/` (object-level authorization in the queries) and
`routes/messages/messages-routes.ts`. The UI side is in `frontend/AGENTS.md` §
Messaging.
